risk_assessments.hazard: Entanglement in mooring lines, slips and falls, crush injuries
risk_assessments.risk_description: Crew working with heavy mooring lines under tension. Risk of line snap, entanglement, or falling overboard during operations.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Use proper PPE (gloves, safety shoes, high-vis vest)
• Maintain clear snap-back zones
• Use radio communication between deck and bridge
• Conduct pre-operation safety briefing
• Ensure adequate lighting for night operations
• Regular inspection of mooring equipment
risk_assessments.notes: High-risk activity requiring constant vigilance. All crew must be trained in mooring procedures.

risk_assessments.activity_task: Working at Heights - Mast and Rigging Inspection
risk_assessments.hazard: Falls from height, equipment failure, weather conditions
risk_assessments.risk_description: Crew working aloft for inspection and maintenance of mast, rigging, and navigation equipment. Risk of falling from height.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Use certified fall arrest harness and double lanyards
• Conduct pre-climb equipment inspection
• Weather conditions must be favorable (wind <15 knots)
• Spotter on deck at all times
• Tool bags secured to prevent dropped objects
• Emergency descent plan in place
risk_assessments.notes: Only qualified personnel with working at heights certification permitted.

risk_assessments.hazard: Fire, explosion, fuel spill, environmental pollution
risk_assessments.risk_description: Transfer of diesel fuel from shore facility to vessel tanks. Risk of spills, fire, or explosion due to fuel vapors.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• No smoking policy enforced
• Fire extinguishers positioned and ready
• Spill kit on deck
• Engine shut down during fueling
• Constant monitoring of fuel transfer
• Bonding cable connected
• VHF radio on emergency channel
• Crew briefed on emergency procedures
risk_assessments.notes: Critical operation requiring full attention. All safety protocols must be followed without exception.

risk_assessments.hazard: Slips, trips and falls, falling overboard, crush injuries
risk_assessments.risk_description: Passengers boarding and disembarking vessel via gangway. Risk of falls, especially for elderly or mobility-impaired passengers.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Non-slip surfaces on gangway
• Handrails on both sides
• Crew assistance available
• Clear signage and instructions
• Adequate lighting
• Safety briefing before departure
• Life jackets accessible
• Supervision during boarding
risk_assessments.notes: Special attention required for passengers with mobility issues or young children.

risk_assessments.hazard: Burns from hot surfaces, noise exposure, confined space, machinery hazards
risk_assessments.risk_description: Working in engine room with hot machinery, high noise levels, and confined spaces. Risk of burns, hearing damage, and entrapment.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Mandatory hearing protection (ear plugs/muffs)
• Heat-resistant gloves when touching hot surfaces
• Proper ventilation maintained
• Machinery guards in place
• Two-person rule for confined space entry
• Emergency communication system
• Regular noise level monitoring
risk_assessments.notes: Engine room entry procedures must be followed. All personnel must be familiar with emergency shutdown procedures.

risk_assessments.hazard: Chain under tension, crush injuries, finger/hand injuries, slips
risk_assessments.risk_description: Operating anchor windlass and handling anchor chain. Heavy equipment under high tension with risk of serious injury.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Keep clear of chain and windlass when in operation
• Use remote control from safe distance
• Wear steel-toed boots and gloves
• Clear communication with bridge
• Emergency stop readily accessible
• Area cordoned off during operations
• Pre-operation inspection of windlass
risk_assessments.notes: High consequence activity. Never work alone. Maintain constant communication with bridge.

risk_assessments.activity_task: Working with Chemicals - Cleaning and Maintenance
risk_assessments.hazard: Chemical exposure, skin/eye irritation, inhalation hazards
risk_assessments.risk_description: Use of cleaning chemicals, degreasers, and maintenance products. Risk of chemical burns, respiratory irritation, or allergic reactions.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Safety Data Sheets (SDS) available and reviewed
• Appropriate PPE (gloves, goggles, respirator if needed)
• Adequate ventilation during use
• Chemicals properly labeled and stored
• Spill kit available
• Emergency eyewash accessible
• Never mix chemicals
• Proper disposal procedures
risk_assessments.notes: Training required before handling chemicals. Keep SDS readily accessible.

risk_assessments.hazard: Collision, grounding, navigation error, equipment failure
risk_assessments.risk_description: Operating vessel in channels, ports, and restricted waterways with increased traffic and limited maneuvering space.
risk_assessments.control_measures:
• Proper passage planning
• All navigation equipment operational and checked
• Additional lookout posted
• Reduced speed appropriate to conditions
• Bridge team fully briefed
• VHF monitoring port operations channel
• Electronic chart system with alarms active
• Master on bridge during critical phases
risk_assessments.notes: Master must be on bridge. Passage plan reviewed before departure.

incidents.title: Slip on wet deck
incidents.description: Crew member nearly slipped on wet deck during morning operations. No injury occurred but could have been serious.
incidents.witnesses: Captain John Masters, First Mate Sarah Thompson
incidents.immediate_actions: Area cordoned off, non-slip mats installed, crew briefed on wet deck procedures
incidents.root_cause: Inadequate drainage in that section of deck, morning dew accumulation
incidents.corrective_actions: Installed additional drainage, improved anti-slip surface treatment
incidents.preventive_actions: Morning deck inspection checklist updated, crew training on wet weather procedures

incidents.title: Engine cooling system malfunction
incidents.description: Starboard engine cooling system failed during transit, causing temperature spike. Engine was shut down immediately to prevent damage.
incidents.witnesses: Chief Engineer David Chen, Second Engineer Michael Roberts
incidents.immediate_actions: Engine shut down, auxiliary cooling activated, vessel proceeded on port engine
incidents.root_cause: Coolant pump impeller failure due to wear
incidents.corrective_actions: Replaced coolant pump and impeller, full system flush performed
incidents.preventive_actions: Increased coolant pump inspection frequency, added to preventive maintenance schedule

incidents.title: Hand injury during mooring operations
incidents.description: Deckhand sustained hand injury when mooring line slipped. Fingers caught between line and bollard.
incidents.injury_details: Laceration and contusion to right hand, two fingers. Required medical attention, 5 stitches. Expected recovery: 2-3 weeks.
incidents.immediate_actions: First aid administered, injured crew member evacuated to shore medical facility, operations temporarily suspended
incidents.root_cause: Insufficient crew on mooring station, fatigue factor (end of long shift), inadequate glove protection
incidents.corrective_actions: Minimum 3 crew on mooring operations, proper safety gloves mandatory, improved supervision
incidents.preventive_actions: Updated mooring procedures, additional crew training, fatigue management review, new cut-resistant gloves ordered

incidents.title: Minor oil leak detected
incidents.description: Small hydraulic oil leak discovered in deck machinery. Approximately 200ml of hydraulic fluid leaked onto deck before detected.
incidents.immediate_actions: Leak contained with absorbent pads, area cleaned, machinery shut down, environmental spill kit deployed

incidents.title: Near collision with recreational vessel
incidents.description: Recreational vessel crossed bow at close range without radio contact. Evasive action taken to avoid collision.
incidents.witnesses: Officer of the Watch, Lookout, Master (called to bridge)
incidents.immediate_actions: Hard turn to starboard, reduced speed, sounded warning signal, reported to VTS
incidents.root_cause: Recreational vessel operator inattention, possible lack of VHF radio monitoring

emergency_procedures.title: Fire Emergency Response Procedure
emergency_procedures.procedure_steps:
1. Sound general alarm (7 short blasts + 1 long blast)
2. Announce "FIRE, FIRE, FIRE" on PA system with location
3. Master to assume command, proceed to bridge
4. Crew to muster stations as per fire plan
5. Fire team don firefighting gear and breathing apparatus
6. Locate and assess fire
7. Attack fire using appropriate extinguishing agent
8. Boundary cooling of adjacent spaces
9. Activate fixed fire suppression if required
10. Continue firefighting until fire is extinguished
11. Post fire watch for minimum 4 hours
12. Investigate cause and complete incident report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: Fire extinguishers (CO2, foam, dry powder), Fire hoses, Breathing apparatus, Firefighting suits, Thermal imaging camera, Boundary cooling equipment
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: Master, Chief Engineer, Fire Team Leader

emergency_procedures.title: Man Overboard Recovery Procedure
emergency_procedures.procedure_steps:
1. Shout "MAN OVERBOARD" - note side (port/starboard)
2. Throw lifebuoy with smoke signal toward person
3. Continuous pointing at person in water
4. Sound alarm - 3 long blasts
5. Announce on PA: "Man Overboard - Port/Starboard Side"
6. Wheel hard over toward side of person (Williamson Turn)
7. Stop engines when person alongside
8. Deploy rescue boat or rescue swimmer
9. Use rescue basket/ladder for recovery
10. Provide first aid and medical assessment
11. Account for all crew
12. Complete incident report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: Lifebuoys with lights and smoke signals, Rescue boat, Rescue ladder/basket, Life jackets, Throw lines, First aid equipment
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: Master, Officer of Watch, Boat Crew

emergency_procedures.title: Medical Emergency Response Procedure
emergency_procedures.procedure_steps:
1. Assess patient - ABC (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)
2. Call for First Aider/Medic
3. Announce medical emergency on PA if needed
4. Provide immediate first aid
5. Contact medical advice via radio/phone
6. Prepare medical report: symptoms, vital signs, treatment given
7. If serious: request medical evacuation
8. Coordinate with shore medical facilities
9. Prepare for evacuation (helicopter/rescue boat)
10. Continue treatment and monitoring
11. Document all actions and treatments
12. Complete medical incident report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: First aid kits, AED (Automated External Defibrillator), Stretcher, Oxygen equipment, Medical reference guides, Radio/satellite phone
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: First Aider, Master, Maritime Medical Advisor (via radio)

emergency_procedures.title: Vessel Grounding Emergency Procedure
emergency_procedures.procedure_steps:
1. Stop engines immediately
2. Sound general alarm
3. Master to bridge
4. Check for hull damage and water ingress
5. Sound all tanks and spaces
6. Assess position, tide, weather
7. Calculate time to high tide
8. Do NOT attempt to refloat without damage assessment
9. Contact coastal radio and report position
10. Request salvage assessment if needed
11. Prepare anchors for kedging if required
12. Monitor for stability and list
13. Prepare for evacuation if necessary
14. Complete grounding report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: Sounding equipment, Damage control equipment, Pumps, Anchors, Radio equipment
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: Master, Chief Engineer, AMSA, Salvage Company

2. Call for First Aider/Medic
3. Announce medical emergency on PA if needed
4. Provide immediate first aid
5. Contact medical advice via radio/phone
6. Prepare medical report: symptoms, vital signs, treatment given
7. If serious: request medical evacuation
8. Coordinate with shore medical facilities
9. Prepare for evacuation (helicopter/rescue boat)
10. Continue treatment and monitoring
11. Document all actions and treatments
12. Complete medical incident report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: First aid kits, AED (Automated External Defibrillator), Stretcher, Oxygen equipment, Medical reference guides, Radio/satellite phone
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: First Aider, Master, Maritime Medical Advisor (via radio)

emergency_procedures.title: Vessel Grounding Emergency Procedure
emergency_procedures.procedure_steps:
1. Stop engines immediately
2. Sound general alarm
3. Master to bridge
4. Check for hull damage and water ingress
5. Sound all tanks and spaces
6. Assess position, tide, weather
7. Calculate time to high tide
8. Do NOT attempt to refloat without damage assessment
9. Contact coastal radio and report position
10. Request salvage assessment if needed
11. Prepare anchors for kedging if required
12. Monitor for stability and list
13. Prepare for evacuation if necessary
14. Complete grounding report
emergency_procedures.equipment_required: Sounding equipment, Damage control equipment, Pumps, Anchors, Radio equipment
emergency_procedures.key_contacts: Master, Chief Engineer, AMSA, Salvage Company

emergency_drills.participants: Master, Chief Engineer, 6 crew members (full complement)
emergency_drills.observations: All crew responded quickly to alarm. Fire team correctly donned BA and located simulated fire. Good coordination between bridge and fire team. All safety procedures followed correctly.
emergency_drills.areas_for_improvement: BA communication could be improved - one team member had radio issues. Need to check all BA equipment before next drill. Response time good but could be 30 seconds faster with more practice.

emergency_drills.participants: All crew (8 persons) and 20 volunteer passengers
emergency_drills.observations: Muster was orderly. All passengers located their lifejackets quickly. Liferaft deployment procedure demonstrated. Passengers briefed on survival procedures. EPIRB and SART operation explained.
emergency_drills.areas_for_improvement: Some passengers confused about muster station location - need clearer signage. One crew member forgot to bring passenger list. Liferaft hydrostatic release needs maintenance check.

emergency_drills.observations: Quick response to alarm. Williamson turn executed perfectly. Dummy recovered in 8 minutes. Good use of lifebuoy and smoke signal. Crew maintained visual contact throughout.
emergency_drills.areas_for_improvement: Recovery ladder deployment was slow - needs practice. One crew member unsure of their role - review emergency procedure assignments.
